blocks.text: In this chapter, students will learn the concept of hypothesis testing and its role in data analysis. They will understand what a hypothesis is and how research questions are converted into testable hypotheses. The chapter introduces different types of hypotheses, including the null hypothesis (H₀), and explains how to formulate correct hypotheses. Students will explore key concepts such as test statistics, critical regions, and p-values, and learn their importance in decision-making. They will follow the step-by-step process of hypothesis testing through simple numerical examples. The chapter also highlights the role of data visualization in presenting and linking results with hypotheses. In addition, students will learn about ethical issues such as bias and responsible use of data. By the end of this chapter, students will be able to interpret results and communicate conclusions clearly.

Hypothesis testing is a method used to make decisions using data. It checks whether an assumption is true or false. This method is widely used in research and analysis. Hypothesis testing follows a clear process that helps accept or reject assumptions. Data is collected and analyzed carefully. This method reduces guesswork as it supports evidence-based decisions.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Hypothesis testing checks assumptions using data. It helps decide whether a claim is true. This method is used in research and experiments. It reduces guesswork. Results depend on proper testing.

A hypothesis is an assumption or statement in research that is made before testing begins. The statement can be tested using data. A hypothesis predicts an outcome; therefore, must be clear and measurable. Data is used to check it. A correct hypothesis guides analysis. It helps focus the study.

items: hθ(x): The hypothesis function with parameters (θ) applied to input (x).
(x): The input features or data points (e.g., attributes of a dataset).
(y): The predicted output or target value (the model's prediction for the given input).
(θ): Parameters or weights of the model (for example, coefficients in a linear regression model).

blocks.text: Research questions define what is being studied. A hypothesis is formed from the research question. Questions guide data collection. Hypotheses provide possible answers. Clear questions lead to clear hypotheses. Both are closely connected. Good research starts with good questions. Hypotheses make the analysis focused. They improve study direction.
Role of Hypothesis Testing in Data Analysis

Hypothesis testing helps analyze data logically to check whether results are meaningful. Testing avoids random conclusions. It compares results with expectations. Hypothesis testing supports accuracy, which is used in experiments and surveys. Decisions are based on evidence. This method improves confidence in results.
